subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate idiomatic expression that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

He is very strict with his students but __good-natured__.

options.text: his eyes are bigger than his stomach
his heart is in the right place

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"good-natured"** means having a kind and friendly disposition. (अच्छे स्वभाव का)

 
 
• **Example: **Despite his strict rules,** his good-natured approach** makes him popular among students.
 
 
 
• **"His heart is in the right place"** is an idiom meaning that someone has good intentions or means well, even if their actions sometimes seem harsh. (उसका दिल सही जगह पर है)
 
 
• **Example: **He can be a tough teacher, but **his heart is in the right place.**
 
 

Hence, we can infer that the most appropriate idiomatic expression for **'good-natured'** is **'his heart is in the right place'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **His eyes are bigger than his stomach** (उसकी आँखें उसके पेट से बड़ी हैं): Describes someone who takes more food than they can eat.

 
 
• **Example:** He ordered a huge meal, but **his eyes were bigger than his stomach.**
 
 
 
• **He has a big mouth **(उसका मुंह बड़ा है): Describes someone who talks too much, often revealing secrets.
 
 
• **Example: **You have to be careful around him, **he has a big mouth.**
 
 
 
• **His heart misses a beat** (उसका दिल एक धड़कन मिस करता है): Describes a sudden feeling of fear or excitement.
 
 
• **Example:** **His heart missed a beat** when he saw the unexpected surprise.
 
 

380:Tdb0,

The correct answer is **Option 2)**
